newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom hits low on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom hits low on profit-taking.

text.p: Shares in Germany's Deutsche Telekom AG on Monday slipped to their lowest level since flotation late last year as dealers said investors, particularly in the U.S., took profits.
Telekom shares slipped to a low of 29.80 marks in IBIS post-bourse electronic trade, 51 pfennigs down on the day.
The shares had earlier closed bourse trade down seven pfennigs at 30.45, still some seven percent up on Telekom's flotation offer price of 28.50 marks.
Dealers said the share fall was more due to a bout of profit-taking than a reaction to the barrage of analyst reports that had followed the expiry of a regulatory gag on Friday.

"The analyst reports weren't bad at all, not as bad as some had been expecting," said one dealer at a Munich-based bank. He added however that U.S. investors appeared to be taking little notice of analysis coming from German banks.

Earlier, the three main underwriters of the stock at flotation were divided in their recommendations, with the two German banks involved taking a more positive view than their United States counterpart, Goldman Sachs.
The consensus view among analysts appeared to be that Deutsche Telekom was fairly valued at around 30 marks, with room for some further growth over the next six months.
